title: esop valuation distribution cycle blank instrument
instruction:
You are Javier Rivenburgh, the valuation analyst supporting Saltmarsh Press, an entirely ESOP-owned client whose 31 December share valuation drives allocations, diversification elections, and retiree distributions. Eamon Rasmussen in benefits is running the annual cycle alone this year, and he needs something he can work from rather than another explanation of the process. The source workbook `saltmarsh_esop_cycle_source.xlsx` contains the authoritative dates, milestone facts, named handoff parties, trustee availability, payroll cutoffs, audit timing, Form 5500 extension timing, election-window assumption, and distribution assumptions for this cycle; use it as the only source for dates and factual values. Please create `saltmarsh_esop_cycle_plan.pptx`, `saltmarsh_esop_cycle_tracker.xlsx`, and `saltmarsh_esop_handoff_brief.docx`, and write all three files into the top level of the working directory where you start, using exactly those filenames.

The package needs to turn the annual valuation-to-distribution cycle into a dated weekly plan that Eamon can execute and that a frontline benefits or payroll employee can pick up without a separate training session. The deck should make the chosen sequence easy to follow from the valuation work through trustee approval, allocation, election letters, the statutory election window, and distributions. It should show what happens each week, what Eamon is waiting for, who supplies it, which activity cannot begin until another one is complete, and where a missed handoff would put the cycle at risk. The order is not prescribed for you. Make a bounded professional choice about how to handle the three-week June collision among the payroll cutoffs, the Form 5500 extension work, and the plan-audit sample, and make that choice visible with its rationale rather than leaving it implicit. Keep the narrative practical: Eamon should be able to identify the next action, the next person or organisation he needs, and the gate that must be cleared.

Use the tracker as the working instrument rather than as a second presentation. It will be opened during the cycle, printed when needed, and updated as work arrives. Planned dates and source-derived milestone descriptions can be present so that the user knows what the rows mean, but the fields for actual completion, current status, waiting detail, handoff confirmation, owner comments, and exceptions must be empty when delivered; do not fill them with examples, sample names, dummy dates, or reassuring placeholder text. Give the user a small controlled vocabulary for status instead of inviting inconsistent free-text labels, and make any calculated field visibly depend on other cells in the workbook rather than asking the user to type the same fact twice. A user-entered actual date should be able to drive the related completion or variance indication, while an unfinished row should remain visibly unfinished. Include a short key or instruction area explaining the status choices and the meaning of any visual signal. The working pages must print cleanly, with no clipped columns or unreadable notes, even though fitting the full dependency picture and the numerical date information on a usable page will require judgement about emphasis and density.

The handoff brief is for the person who receives an action from Eamon or covers for him. It should explain the purpose of the cycle, the roles represented in the source, the meaning of each gate, how to recognise that an item is waiting on another party, how the selected June sequence protects the downstream dates, and what to record when an expected handoff is late or incomplete. It should point the reader to the deck and tracker by their exact filenames. Leave sign-off, exception narrative, and post-cycle review areas blank for actual use; this is not a completed case file. Across the three files, preserve the same milestone names, dates, dependencies, owners, status terms, and June decision. Do not invent a second timetable, add unsupported regulatory requirements, or substitute generic annual-plan language for the facts in the source workbook. The package is for one client and one annual cycle, so keep it focused, professional, and usable by someone who needs to execute the next handoff rather than study valuation theory. Render the presentation, spreadsheet, and document so tables, charts, labels, and page content are not clipped or ambiguous.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/saltmarsh_esop_cycle_source.xlsx` — Authoritative source for the annual valuation date, operating dates, milestone descriptions, owners, handoff parties, dependencies, quarterly trustee availability, payroll cutoffs, audit sampling window, Form 5500 extension timing, election-window duration, and distribution timing assumptions.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `saltmarsh_esop_cycle_plan.pptx` — An executable annual ESOP valuation-to-distribution cycle plan presented as a professional deck for Eamon Rasmussen and the frontline benefits and payroll users who will execute it. (Use the source workbook for all dates and factual values. Show the selected sequence, weekly work, waiting points, owners, handoffs, dependencies, decision gates, June collision management, assumptions, and escalation cues. The deck must remain readable when presented and when exported to PDF. It must contain a clearly identified blank action or exception area for later use, with no fabricated completion entries or examples.)
- `saltmarsh_esop_cycle_tracker.xlsx` — A blank, editable execution tracker that Eamon can use during the annual cycle to record actual dates, status, waiting items, handoff confirmation, and exceptions. (Use exactly the source-derived milestone vocabulary and dates. Planned fields may be populated from the approved cycle plan, but actual completion, status, waiting detail, handoff confirmation, owner comments, and exception fields must ship blank. Include usable dropdown controls, formulas for derived values rather than independently typed constants, clear instructions, and print settings suitable for a working benefits desk document.)
- `saltmarsh_esop_handoff_brief.docx` — A concise handoff and operating brief that lets a frontline benefits or payroll employee understand the cycle, identify the next dependency, and use the blank tracker without separate coaching. (Keep the brief concise and consistent with the deck and tracker. Explain the purpose, roles, gate logic, status vocabulary, June conflict sequence, escalation expectations, and how to record an exception. Leave sign-off, exception narrative, and post-use review fields blank. Do not introduce dates, owners, or rules that are not supported by the source workbook.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
SALTMARSH PRESS
ANNUAL ESOP CYCLE HANDOFF BRIEF
For Eamon Rasmussen and frontline benefits / payroll coverage • 2026 cycle
Purpose and how to use this brief
This is the handoff guide for Saltmarsh Press’s annual ESOP cycle. The 31 December 2025 valuation anchor drives trustee approval, allocation, diversification elections, and retiree distributions. Use the weekly plan in saltmarsh_esop_cycle_plan.pptx and record live work in saltmarsh_esop_cycle_tracker.xlsx.
Who hands what to whom
Handoff
Receiving party
Gate / expected input
Valuation appraiser → Javier / Eamon
Appraiser draft
Draft before review
Javier → ESOP trustee
Reviewed draft
Q2 approval: 14 Apr
ESOP trustee → Eamon
Approval outcome
Clears allocation
Payroll team → Eamon
Reconciled allocation input
Clears letter release
Benefits operations → participants
Election letters
Release 29 Jun after June collision
Eamon → Payroll team
Approved distribution file
Window outcome and cutoffs
Gate logic and waiting states
A gate is a must-be-complete-before condition. Trustee approval precedes allocation; allocation preparation and reconciliation precede election-letter release; the 30-calendar-day election window (30 Jun–29 Jul 2026) closes before distribution preparation; the distribution payroll cutoff is 31 Jul and release cutoff is 14 Aug. Set Status to Waiting when the named Waiting on party has not supplied the input or the gate is not cleared. Record the missing item and next follow-up in the tracker.
June collision sequence
Selected order: payroll cutoff work (08–12 Jun) → Form 5500 extension work (15–19 Jun; deadline 30 Jun) → plan-audit sample work (22–26 Jun). This protects the earliest payroll cutoff, uses the next week for the extension, and preserves the audit sample window. Election letters release on 29 Jun only after June work and allocation reconciliation are clear.
Tracker status vocabulary
Not started = no work begun. Waiting = external input or gate outstanding. In progress = actively being worked. Complete = finished and handed off. At risk = a cutoff or dependency may be missed. Derived variance is actual completion date minus planned date; blank means no actual date entered.
When a handoff is late or incomplete
Set At risk, identify the waiting party, state what is missing, note the cutoff or gate threatened, and record the follow-up in Owner comments or Exception. Keep Handoff confirmed blank until the recipient acknowledges receipt.
Coverage record — leave blank for live use
Covering employee

Date received

Exception narrative

Escalation outcome

Post-cycle review

Source file: saltmarsh_esop_cycle_source.xlsx

spec.professional_context: A finance and benefits operations package for Saltmarsh Press's annual ESOP valuation, allocation, diversification, and retiree distribution cycle. The primary user is Eamon Rasmussen, who must run the cycle with limited support and hand the resulting actions to frontline payroll and benefits staff.
difficulty_sources: Selecting a defensible sequence when several June activities compete for the same narrow operating window
Making every handoff, dependency, waiting point, and approval gate visible without overwhelming the frontline user
Preserving numerical and date fidelity across a presentation, an editable tracker, and a handoff document
Creating a usable blank instrument in which completion and exception fields remain empty while derived fields calculate from user-entered values

source_workbook.role: Single authoritative source. Generate a clean but realistic workbook containing one annual cycle record set with internally consistent dates and dependencies.
required_facts: Draft valuation prepared by the appraiser
Appraiser draft review and trustee approval gate
Allocation preparation and reconciliation after approval
A statutory election window expressed as a duration in days
Quarterly trustee meeting availability, including the meeting that can approve the draft
Three June weeks containing payroll cutoff work, Form 5500 extension work, and plan-audit sample work
Named roles and handoff parties using only the permitted people and organisations
Source-derived assumptions for business-day or calendar-day interpretation where needed
relationships: Trustee approval cannot precede receipt and review of the appraiser draft.
Allocation preparation cannot begin as an approved activity before trustee approval.
Election letters cannot be released before the allocation inputs are approved and reconciled.
The election window ends after the stated source duration from letter release.
Distribution preparation follows the election-window result and the applicable payroll or distribution cutoff.
The selected June ordering must preserve the source deadlines and expose the competing work rather than silently dropping one activity.
Every milestone has an owner and a handoff or waiting party derived from the source.

slide_schema: source assumptions and annual date spine
weekly roadmap from valuation through distribution
blank action and exception capture area
required_objects: At least one timeline or roadmap object with weekly labels
At least one dependency or gate visual
A visible legend for status or risk signalling
A visibly blank action/exception capture area

cycle_tracker_schema.derived_field: Derived variance must be a formula based on the planned date and actual completion date, or equivalent source-supported date inputs, and must not be an independently typed constant.
affordances: Date and numeric formats appropriate to the source
Conditional formatting that distinguishes status choices without relying on colour alone
Print area, page size, orientation, fit-to-width, and repeated header settings that keep the tracker usable on paper

xlsx.lists_schema: Contains only the controlled status and handoff values used by validation; no sample transaction or completion data.
xlsx.instructions_schema: Explains purpose, blank-field use, status vocabulary, derived variance meaning, exception recording, and relationship to the deck and brief.

docx.purpose: Short handoff guide for an untrained frontline user.
required_sections: blank sign-off and post-cycle review fields

gold_derivation.method: Create the source workbook offline, derive the accepted dependency graph and date relationships from it, and author all three deliverables from the same generated source record set. Permit professional variation in visual design and wording while requiring relational agreement with the source.
gold_derivation.intended_verdict: Pass when the package is a coherent, dated, source-faithful blank instrument with a defensible June sequence, intact gate logic, usable affordances, and no fabricated completion data.

reference_files.purpose: Authoritative source for the annual valuation date, operating dates, milestone descriptions, owners, handoff parties, dependencies, quarterly trustee availability, payroll cutoffs, audit sampling window, Form 5500 extension timing, election-window duration, and distribution timing assumptions.
reference_files.discovery: Use this workbook as the sole supplied source of dates and cycle facts. It is placed in the working directory before work begins.

deliverables.description: An executable annual ESOP valuation-to-distribution cycle plan presented as a professional deck for Eamon Rasmussen and the frontline benefits and payroll users who will execute it.
constraints: Use the source workbook for all dates and factual values. Show the selected sequence, weekly work, waiting points, owners, handoffs, dependencies, decision gates, June collision management, assumptions, and escalation cues. The deck must remain readable when presented and when exported to PDF. It must contain a clearly identified blank action or exception area for later use, with no fabricated completion entries or examples.

deliverables.description: A blank, editable execution tracker that Eamon can use during the annual cycle to record actual dates, status, waiting items, handoff confirmation, and exceptions.
constraints: Use exactly the source-derived milestone vocabulary and dates. Planned fields may be populated from the approved cycle plan, but actual completion, status, waiting detail, handoff confirmation, owner comments, and exception fields must ship blank. Include usable dropdown controls, formulas for derived values rather than independently typed constants, clear instructions, and print settings suitable for a working benefits desk document.

deliverables.description: A concise handoff and operating brief that lets a frontline benefits or payroll employee understand the cycle, identify the next dependency, and use the blank tracker without separate coaching.
constraints: Keep the brief concise and consistent with the deck and tracker. Explain the purpose, roles, gate logic, status vocabulary, June conflict sequence, escalation expectations, and how to record an exception. Leave sign-off, exception narrative, and post-use review fields blank. Do not introduce dates, owners, or rules that are not supported by the source workbook.
